d: Quick answers about setup, Cora Max, Cora Mobile, devices, alerts, Reef Buddy and Cora Assistant, languages, and your account.
b: Short answers here, with links to the full pages. If your question is really "something looks wrong", go straight to Troubleshooting . Getting started What do I need to buy to use Cora? Just a phone. Cora Mobile runs your tanks, devices and alerts on its own. Cora Max is an optional wall screen for the reef room. More in Cora Help . Do I need a Cora Max, or can I use just the phone app? The phone app is enough. Every core feature (tanks, devices, dashboards, alerts, dosing) is in Cora Mobile. Cora Max shows the same tanks on a bigger screen and adds voice. See Cora Help and Setting up Cora Mobile . How do I add my first tank? Cora Mobile walks you through it. Create your account, add a tank, and answer its profile questions. Devices and dashboards come after that. More in Setting up Cora Mobile . What does "tank profile" mean and why does it ask so many questions? The tank profile describes your system: size, water type, livestock, and how you dose and test. Cora uses your answers to set sensible starting thresholds, and to make Reef Buddy and Cora Assistant talk about your tank instead of reefs in general. More in Tank profile . How long does setup take? One tank with no equipment takes a few minutes. Each real device (probe, controller, pump) needs its own pairing step, so that part takes longer. You can always add more later. More in Setting up Cora Mobile . Cora Max Can one Cora Max show more than one tank? Yes. One Cora Max can show every tank on your account, one at a time, and the Reef Room shows them all together. What is "Primary Cora Max" and do I need to set it? It decides which Cora Max talks to a tank's local equipment. Most people never touch it. With one Cora Max there's nothing to choose, and the default, Any active (automatic) , lets every online Cora Max share the job. Pick a specific one only if you want a single device doing the polling. More in More than one Cora device . Which device answers "Hey Cora" if I have more than one Cora Max? Only one Cora device answers the wake phrase at a time. You choose it in Settings under Cora Assistant . Primary Cora Max is a separate setting for talking to your equipment. See Voice on Cora Max and More than one Cora device . Does Cora Max need the internet to work, or just my home Wi-Fi? Both. It needs your home Wi-Fi to reach your equipment, and an internet connection to reach Cora Cloud for sign-in, sync and the Assistant. The status tag in the top bar shows which one it has right now. More in The Cora Max home screen . Does Cora Max keep working if Cora Cloud is unreachable? Partly. It keeps showing the last data it has and keeps working with equipment on its own network. Sign-in, sync between devices and the Assistant wait until Cora Cloud is back. See The Cora Max home screen and Devices and device health . Can I move my Cora Max to a different Wi-Fi network later? Yes. On Cora Max, join the new network in its own network settings. Your tanks, devices and account stay the same. Only the Wi-Fi connection changes. More in Setting up Cora Max . Phone app Why does Cora Mobile ask for Local Network and Bluetooth access? It needs Local Network access to find and pair a Cora Max or Wi-Fi equipment on your home network, and Bluetooth for equipment that pairs over Bluetooth. Without them, pairing can't find the device. See Settings and Troubleshooting . Can two Cora Max screens show the same tank? Yes. Add both to the same tank and they show the same live data. Primary Cora Max only decides which one talks to the local equipment. Both can still show the tank. More in More than one Cora device . Can I check on my tank from my phone when I'm not home? Yes. Your readings and history are always there through Cora Cloud, wherever you are. A few device settings only open while your phone is on the same network as the device. More in More than one Cora device . Can I control equipment, like turning off a pump, when I'm away from home? For most equipment, yes. Outlets, feed mode and similar controls go through Cora Cloud, so they work when you're away. A few of the device's own settings still need your phone on the tank's Wi-Fi. See More than one Cora device and Controlling your equipment . Can two people use the same tank? Right now Cora works with one account per tank. If someone else needs to see or help with a tank, share it with them. Don't sign in to the same account on two phones. More in Sharing . Devices and integrations What equipment does Cora work with? A growing list of controllers and equipment, from Wi-Fi controllers to dosing pumps and gyres. For anything Cora doesn't connect to, you can log readings by hand. The current list is in Connections . Is Cora affiliated with Neptune, Red Sea, Jebao, GHL, HYDROS, or Maxspect? No. Cora isn't affiliated with, endorsed by, or partnered with any manufacturer it connects to. That includes Maxspect, GHL and HYDROS, whose integrations are still in beta. Cora talks to their public accounts, official APIs or local network protocols. A manufacturer's own app or firmware update can change or break that connection at any time, without notice. More in Connections . What does it mean when an integration is "beta"? It means we're still testing and developing it. Some readings or controls may be limited, and what you see can change between updates. Maxspect, GHL and HYDROS are all beta today. If something doesn't work as the guide describes, let us know from Getting help . Why can't Cora Mobile find my Cora Max when I try to pair it? It's almost always Wi-Fi. Your phone and Cora Max need to be on the same network to pair, and on iPhone, Cora also needs Local Network access. Cora Mobile shows which pairing step failed and gives you a Retry button. More in Troubleshooting . Does my phone need to be on the same Wi-Fi as my Cora Max? To pair, yes. After that, everyday use works from anywhere through Cora Cloud. Only a few of the device's own settings need your phone back on that Wi-Fi. See More than one Cora device and Troubleshooting . What happens if I change my Wi-Fi router or network name? Any equipment or Cora Max on that network goes out of reach until it joins the new network or name. Reconnect each device the same way you first added it. More in Troubleshooting . My device found nothing when I searched for equipment, what's wrong? Check that the equipment is powered on and already set up in the manufacturer's app, if it needs one. Then check that your phone allows Local Network and Bluetooth access. Cora can't find equipment that has never joined your network. See Settings and Troubleshooting . Why did my Red Sea device's readings stop updating? When nothing on that tank's network is polling your Red Sea equipment, Cora shows a banner saying no device is reading it. Check Primary Cora Max in Settings, or open the tank on a device on the same Wi-Fi as the Red Sea gear. See Troubleshooting and More than one Cora device . Why does it say "Could not reach the pump" when I try to control my Jecod pump? The command didn't get to the pump. Usually it's off, off its network, or (for a Bluetooth-only pump) out of range. Check power and connection, move closer if it uses Bluetooth, and try again. More in Troubleshooting . Why does the gyre program not apply? Sending a schedule to a gyre can fail just like a command, because the gyre didn't respond. Check it's powered on and on its network, then try again from the schedule screen. See Scheduling equipment and Troubleshooting . Is it safe to let Cora control my dosing pump automatically? Cora only doses what you set up: a product, a strength and a schedule you define. If a dose stops partway, Cora raises an alert about it. It doesn't assume the dose finished, so nothing gets under- or overdosed without you knowing. See Dosing and Controlling your equipment . What happens if a dose is interrupted halfway through? Cora raises an alert saying the dose didn't finish and, when it can tell, how much went in. Read that alert before you assume the full dose was delivered, then resume or adjust. More in Controlling your equipment . How does Cora know how strong my dosing product is? It comes from the built-in product library, which lists salts and dosing products with their published figures. If you add your own product, you enter the strength yourself. More in Dosing . Alerts and notifications Why am I not getting notifications at all? Check that the alert's category is allowed to send notifications under Settings → Notifications . Then check your phone's own notification permission for Cora. The daily briefing also stays quiet on days when nothing changed. That's normal. See Notifications and Troubleshooting . Why is an alert not clearing even though the reading looks fine? There are three usual causes. The reading is still out of range (check its history), the threshold doesn't suit your tank, or the source is reporting an out-of-range number (often a probe that needs calibrating). Usually you should fix the source and leave the threshold alone. See Alerts and thresholds and Troubleshooting . How do I silence an alert temporarily without turning it off? On Cora Max, tap Snooze . It mutes that alert on that screen for the cooldown set on the alert rule. The alert stays open and its threshold doesn't change. On your phone, set a longer Cooldown between alerts on the rule instead. More in Alerts and thresholds . What's the difference between snoozing an alert and dismissing it? Both are on Cora Max and only affect that screen. Snooze mutes the alert there for a while, and it comes back if the problem is still there when the snooze ends. Dismiss closes it there until the reading is back in range. If the problem comes back later, you'll get a new alert. More in Alerts and thresholds . Can I set how long an alert stays snoozed, is a week the longest? The snooze lasts as long as the alert rule's Cooldown between alerts , which you set in Cora Mobile. The longest is 1 week. More in Alerts and thresholds . Why did I get an alert on my phone but not on Cora Max, or vice versa? The switches in Cora Mobile's Settings → Notifications belong to your account, so they apply to every phone you're signed in on. Cora Max has no notification switches. It shows every alert at the wall, unless you've snoozed or dismissed it on that screen. If your phone stays silent, check that the category is switched on and that your phone allows notifications from Cora. See Notifications and Alerts on Cora Max . Reef Buddy and Cora Assistant What can I ask Cora, and what can't it do? Cora Assistant answers questions about your tank's readings, history, dosing and journal. It can also carry out equipment actions you ask for by voice or text. It can't act on anything it has no data or connection for, and it tells you so instead of guessing. More in The Assistant . Can Cora actually control my equipment, or just tell me things? Both. Ask a question and it answers from your tank's data. Ask it to do something, like start feed mode, and it does it if the equipment supports it. See The Assistant and Voice on Cora Max . Does Cora remember what I told it last time? Yes, within the limits on the Assistant page. It can use earlier context about your tank, so you don't have to repeat yourself every time. More in The Assistant . Why did Cora give me a wrong or strange answer? Cora Assistant answers from the data it has for the tank you've selected. The usual causes are the wrong tank selected, missing readings, or a question that could mean two things. Check the tank picker or rephrase, and try again. More in The Assistant . What is Reef Buddy and how is it different from the Assistant? Reef Buddy is your daily briefing, written for you without you asking. It has a headline, two scores and the insights behind them. Cora Assistant is what you ask questions, whenever you like, by typing or talking. See Reef Buddy and the Glossary . Languages What language does Cora speak, and can family members use a different one? Cora uses one language for the whole account. You can't set a different one per person or per device, so everyone signed in to that account sees the same language everywhere. See Settings and the Glossary . I changed the language on my phone, why did my Cora Max change too? Language is an account setting. Change it anywhere (your phone or any Cora Max) and it changes everywhere within moments. See Settings and the Glossary . Will old reports and alerts be translated after I change languages? No. Anything already written stays in its original language. New alerts, reports and Reef Buddy briefings use the new language from then on. See Settings and the Glossary . Account, plans and privacy What's free forever, and what needs a subscription? Plans can change, so we don't list them here. The current plans, their limits and what each includes are on the Plans page in Cora Mobile and in Plans . What happens to my data if my trial or subscription ends? Your tank history isn't deleted. What changes is which features you can use. Plans shows exactly what each tier includes. If I delete my Cora account, does that cancel my Apple or Google subscription? No. Deleting your Cora account doesn't cancel a subscription you bought through the App Store or Google Play. Cancel it separately with Apple or Google. More in Settings . Can I change or cancel my plan without losing my tank history? Yes. Your tanks, devices and history stay with your account whatever plan you're on. Only the features you can use change. More in Plans . What does Cora do with my tank data? Cora uses it to show you your readings, run alerts and thresholds, and power Reef Buddy and Cora Assistant. What's stored and how it may be used is covered in Your data , Settings and the privacy policy. Can I get a copy of everything Cora has stored about my tank? Yes, you can export it from Cora Mobile. Your data explains what the export includes and how to ask for it. If I delete my account, is everything really gone? Deleting your account removes your data as described on the Settings page, including the choice about contributing anonymised data. If you want the exact detail, read Settings before you delete. Troubleshooting pointers Why does a widget show no value? It's usually a connection problem. The parameter is still there. Check whether nearby widgets have the same problem, then look at the device's row under Devices . More in Troubleshooting . Why does a reading say it's from an hour ago? Because nothing newer has arrived. Some equipment only reports that often (an hourly titrator, for example). For anything else, check the device's row under Devices . More in Troubleshooting . My device says "sign-in refused", what do I do? The manufacturer's account rejected the saved sign-in. Almost always, the password was changed on their side. Open the device's row and sign in again. More in Troubleshooting . Why does Cora Max show old data even though it says "Online"? Online and Cloud both mean Cora Max itself is fine. If the tag shows either one and the data is still old, the problem is somewhere before Cora Max. Check the same tank on your phone. See Troubleshooting and The Cora Max home screen . Why do my probe and my test kit disagree? Cora is showing you a real disagreement. Nothing is broken. Calibrate the probe, retest with fresh reagent, and compare the two under the same conditions. An ICP result gives you a third number to compare. See Troubleshooting and ICP and health reports . What happens if my internet goes down? Cora Max and Cora Mobile keep showing the last data they received and keep working with equipment already on their own network. Sign-in, sync and the Assistant come back when the connection does. See Troubleshooting and The Cora Max home screen . Does Cora work without internet? Partly. Readings you already have, and control of equipment on the same local network, keep working. Sign-in, sync between devices, Cora Cloud storage and the Assistant need an internet connection. See The Cora Max home screen and Troubleshooting . Still can't find your answer? Troubleshooting goes through fixes symptom by symptom, or you can email cora@coraiq.tech .

d: What Cora means by tank, source, widget, saved design, threshold, insight and other words you'll see.
b: Account language The one language your whole Cora account uses. It isn't set per person or per device. Change it in Settings → Language on your phone or on any Cora Max, and every device follows within moments. New alerts, reports and Reef Buddy briefings use the new language from then on. Anything already written stays in its original language. See Settings . Age How long ago a reading was taken, shown on every parameter widget as now , 1h , 2d . It has nothing to do with when the screen last refreshed. An old age means the reading itself is old. Alert Cora telling you something needs attention. Usually it's a reading outside the range you set. It can also be a parameter moving too fast, an equipment fault, a consumable running low, or a lab result coming in. Most alerts clear by themselves once the problem passes. See Alerts and thresholds . Answering device The Cora device that answers when you say the wake phrase. You pick it in Settings → Cora Assistant . Only one device answers at a time. Primary Cora Max is a different setting. It decides which device talks to your local equipment, and has nothing to do with voice. Automation A rule or scene that runs by itself, like "if temperature goes above 27, turn on the fan". You'll find these in Settings → Automation . On newer Cora Max builds you can also build and edit a scene on Cora Max itself. Calibration Adjusting a probe so its readings match a known reference, usually a calibration solution. Cora records when you last calibrated a probe and can remind you when it's due. See Probes . Cooldown The shortest time Cora waits before sending the same alert again, from 15 minutes to a week. It keeps one ongoing problem from pinging you every few minutes. You set it for each alert rule. See Alerts and thresholds . Cora Cloud The service that keeps your phone, your Cora Max and your equipment in step, and stores your history. Sign-in, syncing between devices and the Assistant all need it. Readings you already have, and equipment already on its own network, keep working without it. Cora Assistant The part of Cora you ask questions. You can type or talk to it on both Cora Mobile and Cora Max. It's also the name of the settings group where you choose the answering device . Cora Max The wall screen for the reef room. It shows your tanks live and you can talk to it. Cora Mobile The phone app. The icon on your home screen says Cora . DŌS head A dosing pump connected to Cora. You can give each head a use (a water change, kalkwasser, a reactor, feeding and more), track it in litres or large containers, and run large-volume doses. If a head loses contact mid-dose, Cora raises a restore alert. It doesn't assume the dose finished. See Controlling your equipment . Dose One delivery of liquid from a DŌS head or another dosing pump, using the product and amount you set. Cora logs every dose so your consumption and history match up. Feed mode A pause for feeding. It stops the right equipment and turns it back on automatically. That's safer than switching pumps off by hand, because you don't have to remember to switch them back on. GHL Short for GHL Advanced Technology, maker of the ProfiLux and Mitras line of controllers. Cora's GHL support is a beta . See Connecting your equipment . Health report A deeper, periodic look at a whole system. It takes every parameter, source, dose and recent lab result into account together. See ICP and health reports . HYDROS CoralVue's controller and dosing ecosystem. Cora reaches it through HYDROS's own cloud, so it keeps working away from home. Cora's HYDROS support is a beta . See Connecting your equipment . ICP A lab water test that covers a wide range of elements. Upload the result and Cora tracks every element over time. Insight One specific point in a Reef Buddy briefing, such as a parameter drifting, two sources disagreeing, or something you haven't tested in a while. Journal Your record of what you did to the tank. Cora reads it too, so you can ask "what did I do before the alkalinity dropped?" and get an answer. See The journal . Outlet A switchable socket on your equipment. In Cora it has three states, Auto , Off and On . Parameter Something you can measure in your water, like alkalinity, calcium, nitrate or temperature. Primary Cora Max The Cora Max that talks to a tank's local equipment (its Wi-Fi and Bluetooth devices) for you. Set it to one Cora Max, or to Any active (automatic) . With that option every online Cora Max for the tank shares the job, and the last write wins. This is separate from the answering device , which is about voice. Primary Cora Max is about polling equipment. Change it in Settings → Primary Cora Max . See More than one Cora device . Saved design A dashboard layout you've kept under My dashboards . You can apply it again later or load it onto another tank or screen. Reef Buddy Your daily briefing. It has a headline, two scores ( Stability out of 100 and Data as a percentage), and the insights behind them. See Reef Buddy . Snooze A button on a Cora Max alert. It mutes the alert on that Cora Max for the rule's cooldown (up to a week) without closing it. Dismiss is the other button. It closes the alert on that Cora Max until the reading is back in range. Your phone's notifications aren't affected by either. See Alerts and thresholds . Source Where a reading came from, whether that's a probe, a controller, a lab result, or you with a test kit. Every reading has one, so Cora can tell you when two sources disagree. If more than one source reports the same reading, Probes is where you choose which one to trust, or leave it Automatic. Tank A body of water you track. Most people have one. A frag system or a quarantine tank counts as a separate tank. Threshold The range you're happy with for a parameter. It can be a range, a ceiling or a floor. You set it. The defaults are only a starting point. Vacation mode Tank-sitter mode. You make a dated plan with a checklist of jobs, and Cora turns it into a read-only page you can share with whoever looks after the tank while you're away. See Settings . Widget One tile on a dashboard that shows one thing. There are eleven types: Value, Gauge, Graph, Status, Outlet, ReefBeat, Apex module, Jecod, Maxspect (beta) , GHL (beta) and HYDROS (beta) . See Widget reference .

d: How to set up and use Cora Max and Cora Mobile, from your first tank to dashboards, devices, alerts, Reef Buddy, ICP and health reports.
b: Everything you need to run your reef with Cora. Choose where you want to start. New to Cora Mobile Create your account, add your first tank, and get readings on screen. New to Cora Max First run, pairing, and getting your tanks onto the big screen. Build your dashboard Pick a layout, add widgets, and arrange them how you like. Fix a problem Readings stopped, a device went quiet, or an alert won't clear. Frequently asked questions Quick answers about setup, Cora Max, devices, alerts, plans and privacy. The two halves of Cora Cora Mobile is the phone app. You set almost everything up here (tanks, devices, dashboards, alerts, dosing products), and it's what you carry when you're away from the tank. The icon on your home screen just says Cora . Cora Max is the wall screen for the reef room. It shows the same tanks and the same live data, big enough to read from across the room, and you can talk to it. Both use the same account. Your tanks, readings, devices and records are the same on each, and you only set them up once. A few things stay with one screen. Each screen has its own dashboard layout . Its Wi-Fi, brightness, audio, wake word and child-lock settings also apply only there. What is shared and what is not explains the difference. Start on your phone Even if you bought Cora Max, set up your tanks and devices in Cora Mobile first. Typing is easier on a phone, and Cora Max picks everything up automatically. What Cora adds to a controller Every reading shows its source and age. If two sources disagree, such as a probe and a test kit or a doser and your ICP results, Cora tells you instead of quietly averaging them. When something starts to drift, Reef Buddy brings it up the next morning. d: Every command your system carried out, refused or couldn't confirm, readable at the wall.
b: Cora Max shows the same activity log as your phone. It lists every actuation request (every attempt to change something) and what happened to it. A refused or unconfirmed request may never have reached the equipment at all, and that's exactly why it's logged. Open it from the tank menu (tap the tank name in the top bar), or go to Settings → Tank settings → [your tank] → Activity . The legend stays at the top of the screen, so you never have to remember what an outcome means. What each entry tells you Each row shows the action, the equipment and the time. Two more details are the ones to look at. What asked for it. You at this screen, you on your phone, voice, the Assistant, an automation rule, a smart button, or your account. If you did it at the wall, the entry says so. How it travelled. Whether the command went over your own network or through your account, and which Cora carried it out. If you have more than one Cora, this tells you which one acted. The four outcomes Outcome Means Confirmed The equipment reported back that it did it Unconfirmed Sent, but nothing reported back. We don't know whether it worked Refused Didn't run. A safety rule, a lock or the equipment itself turned it down No change It was already in the state you asked for Why the outcome matters at the wall When you tap, a command that was sent but never acknowledged looks the same as one that worked. This screen shows you the difference. If something you asked for doesn't seem to have happened, check here before you decide the equipment has failed. Usually the request was refused, or nothing ever reported back. Reading it alongside the journal Activity shows what the system did. The journal shows what you did by hand. Between them, they explain most surprises.

d: Alert tags in the top bar, the notification inbox, and changing thresholds at the wall.
b: Alerts in the top bar When a reading is out of range, it shows up as a small tag in the top bar, big enough to spot from across the room. If there are more than fit, you'll see +2 (or however many). Tap a tag to see them all. When an alert appears at the wall When a reading goes out of range, Cora Max also shows the alert in the middle of the screen. There are three buttons under it. Respond by voice lets you talk to Cora about the alert without typing or tapping anything else. More about this in Talking to Cora . Snooze [duration] silences the alert on this Cora Max for a while. The button shows how long, for example Snooze 1 h . That's the cooldown set for this alert in Cora Mobile's alert settings, and it can be as long as 1 week (handy for something like a low reagent level that won't change for days). Dismiss closes the alert now. It stays quiet on this screen until the reading is back in range. If the problem comes back later, you'll get a new alert. If Snooze or Dismiss shows an error, try once more. If it keeps failing, have a look at Troubleshooting . Snooze only affects this Cora Max While an alert is snoozed or dismissed, this Cora Max stops popping it up, sounding it and speaking it, and it leaves the list in the top bar. Your phone still gets its notifications, other Cora Max screens still show the alert, it stays in Notification history , and your alert settings don't change. The notification inbox Settings → Cora Max Settings → Notifications → Notification history is the inbox for your whole account. It holds every briefing, alarm and account notice for your system, including the ones this screen didn't raise and anything your phone missed. Editing thresholds Each tank has its own journal, maintenance, alerts, livestock and briefing. Tap the tank name in the top bar and choose Alerts , or go to Settings → [your tank] → Alert thresholds . Both open the same ranges you see on your phone, and a change you make here applies everywhere. You can also change a threshold by opening its widget on the dashboard. How ranges and rules work is explained in Alerts and thresholds . One alert for the whole account Each device doesn't raise its own copy of an alert. Cora Max, your phone and any other screen show the same one, and it clears on all of them when the reading is back in range.

d: Building, running and editing scenes right on the Cora Max screen.
b: A scene is a saved set of equipment actions that run together, either for a set time or until you stop it. Scenes work the same whether you build them on your phone or on Cora Max. This page is about doing it at the wall. Where to find scenes Settings → Automations lists every scene for all your tanks. If you have more than one tank, there's a filter chip for each. You'll see the same list whether a scene was built on your phone or on Cora Max. Tap a scene to edit it, or tap + to build a new one. If you have more than one tank and no filter is picked, Cora Max asks which tank the new scene is for. Building a scene Give the scene a name . Add steps . On Cora Max, a step can switch an Apex outlet ( On , Off or Auto ) or a Zigbee plug ( on , off or toggle ). Steps for other equipment that were added on your phone still show up here. You can reorder or remove them, but you can't add new ones like them from this screen. Choose how long it runs. Pick a number of minutes, or permanent (it runs until you stop it). Choose whether the scene asks for confirmation before it runs. Leave this on unless you're sure the scene never touches anything that needs a second look before it changes. Save. DŌS dosing heads are never a scene step No scene can switch on a dosing head, whether you build it on Cora Max or on your phone. A dose shouldn't be something a scene can start by accident. Running a scene Scenes show up as tiles on the dashboard. Tap Run to start one. If the scene needs confirmation, Cora Max first lists what it's about to do, one line per step. Read it, then run it or cancel. While a timed scene runs, its tile counts down to the end and shows a Stop button if you want to end it early. A permanent scene's tile shows it as running until you stop it. Running or stopping a scene always goes through Cora Cloud, like any other command. You'll find the result in What was changed, and by what . If a scene won't run or won't stop, have a look at Troubleshooting . Child lock covers scenes too When Child lock is on, you can't run or stop a scene from this screen, just like every other control. You can still ask about a scene by voice, but you can't start or stop one. Editing or deleting a scene To change a scene's name, steps, duration or confirmation setting, or to delete it, open it from Settings → Automations or long-press its tile on the dashboard. Older Cora Max screens can run a scene but not edit it Building and editing scenes at the wall is new on Cora Max. An older Cora Max on the same account can still show and run a scene made on your phone or on a newer Cora Max. It just can't change it. If that happens, update Cora Max, or edit the scene on your phone or a newer screen. There's more on what scenes can do, and how to build them on your phone, in Scenes and automations .

d: Switching outlets from Cora Max, using feed mode, and what Auto really means.
b: Cora Max can switch the equipment on your system. You can do it from control widgets on the dashboard, from the Outlets & Feed drawer, or by voice. These controls act on your tank There's no undo. Outlets with a padlock ask you to confirm first. The rest change as soon as you tap. A command can come back Confirmed , Unconfirmed (sent, but nothing reported back), Refused or No change . More about this in Controlling your equipment . The three states Every outlet is in one of three states. Auto hands the outlet back to its Apex programming. Most of the time, that's where an outlet should be. Off and On are manual overrides. They take effect right away and stay until you change them back . They don't expire, and nothing resets them for you. A manual override doesn't expire Set it back to Auto when you're done, because nothing else will. An override isn't a lock, though. You, your voice or an automation can still change it later. Switching from the dashboard Control widgets show the three states, with the current one highlighted. Tap the one you want. Some outlets have a padlock . There's nothing to switch off for it. It means the outlet asks you to confirm before it changes, so a stray tap can't switch something critical. There's more on this below. The Controls drawer Pull up the tab at the bottom of the dashboard to open Controls . It shows every outlet on the system, with or without a widget, plus the feed cycles. Feed cycles across the top, then every outlet. An outlet with a padlock needs you to confirm before it changes. When you tap it, a dialog shows the outlet, its current state and the override you're about to set. It's a confirmation step, and there's no lock to turn off somewhere else. Feed mode Feed mode is the safe way to pause flow while you feed. It pauses the equipment that should pause, leaves the rest alone, and puts everything back by itself when time's up. Use it instead of switching pumps off by hand. It puts the system back even if you forget. Feed cycles are lettered A , B , C and D . They're the cycles your controller defines, and each one pauses a different set of equipment. Pick the one that fits what you're doing. Cancel ends a running cycle early and puts everything back right away. Start one from the Controls drawer, or say "start feed mode" . By voice You can switch outlets by voice, for example "turn the skimmer off" or "put the fan back on auto" . Before anything reaches your equipment, Cora checks with you first . It tells you what it's about to do and waits for your OK. If it isn't sure what you asked, it won't act. More about this in Talking to Cora . Seeing what happened Every request is logged, along with what asked for it and how it travelled. The request can come from Cora Mobile, a Cora screen, voice, the Assistant, an automation rule, a smart button or your account. On Cora Max, tap the tank name in the top bar and choose Activity . On your phone, you'll find it in Settings → Activity . When something changed and you don't know why, look there first.

d: Choose a grid, add widgets and save layouts for the Cora Max display.
b: The Cora Max dashboard uses a fixed grid . The display doesn't scroll, so every tile has to fit on one screen. That's the main difference from the phone dashboard. Open the editor from the tank menu (tap the tank name in the top bar, then Dashboard layout ). You'll also find it under Settings → Tank settings → [your tank] → Dashboard layout . Grid sizes across the top, then the tiles. This is a layout screen, so each tile shows its type and source instead of a reading. Nothing is saved until you press Save. You can also edit it from your phone In Cora Mobile, go to Devices → your Cora Max → Edit Dashboard to build the same layout. It's quicker than arranging tiles by hand on a wall screen, and the result shows up on Cora Max right away. Choosing a grid Pick the grid size first. Changing it later moves all the tiles around. Grid Tiles Feels like 2×2, 3×2, 3×3 4–9 Large. Easy to read from across the room. 4×4, 5×3, 6×4 16–24 The usual choice for a full system. 6×5, 8×4, 8×5 30–40 Dense. A whole reef room on one screen. 9×5, 10×5 45–50 Very dense. Best on the largest screens. Auto up to 32 Cora picks a shape that fits however many tiles you've added. A fixed grid holds as many tiles as it has cells, up to 50 on 10×5. Auto has its own limit of 32 tiles. Past that, the text gets too small to read from a distance. Not sure? Start with Auto Add the tiles you want and leave the grid on Auto . Cora picks a shape that fits them. If you like it, you can switch to that fixed shape afterwards. Changing the grid only drops tiles when they don't fit When you change the grid, Cora doesn't throw tiles away by position. Tiles that still have a valid cell stay where they are, and the rest are packed back in, in order. You only lose tiles when the new grid has fewer cells than you have tiles , and Cora tells you how many went. Going from 10×5 (50 cells) to 3×3 (9) loses most of them. Adding and arranging The three gestures are listed along the top of the editor: tap a tile to edit , long-press to move it , and ✕ to remove it . A tile can be one or two cells wide and one or two cells tall. Outlets & Feed adds all your controllable outlets and feed cycles in one go. Clear all empties the grid so you can start over. The eleven tile types are Value, Gauge, Graph, Status, Outlet, ReefBeat, Apex module, Jecod, Maxspect (beta) , GHL (beta) and HYDROS (beta) . You'll find them all in the Widget reference . Designing for distance People read a wall display from further away than a phone, and usually with a quick glance. Make your key parameters two by two. Alkalinity, temperature and pH are things you'll want to read without walking over. Put controls at the edges. Outlet tiles are the ones you reach for, and they're easier to hit at the sides. Group tiles by subject. Keep everything about dosing together and everything about flow together, because you scan a wall by area. Keep trace elements small. They and other slow-moving numbers are for reference, so a one-by-one value tile is plenty. Saving layouts Nothing you do in the editor takes effect until you press Save . If you leave without saving, your changes are lost. My dashboards keeps layouts you want to come back to, so you can switch instead of rebuilding. For example, you might want a dense everyday layout and a big-tile one for when you're working in the tank. Switching takes one tap. Multiple tanks Each tank has its own layout. Edit each one from that tank's own settings.

d: Device pages on the big screen for probes, outlets, dosing heads, testers and pumps.
b: Cora Max reaches the same equipment as your phone, and each device has its own page. Open one from Settings → Devices , or tap a device tile on the dashboard. Feed cycles and every outlet, laid out for a wall screen. These controls act on live equipment There's no preview and no undo. A command goes out the moment you tap, but sending it doesn't mean it's done. It comes back Confirmed , Unconfirmed , Refused or No change , and you can see which in Activity . What has a page Device Shows Neptune Apex Probes and outlets, and you can switch each outlet Trident Test state, reagent and waste levels, and a button to start a test DŌS , including the DŌS QD Each head's dosing, schedule, runway and container volume (with pause, fill, dose now and a one-time twenty-second measure) Red Sea ReefBeat Whatever the unit has: dosing heads, reservoir, roller days, pump mode, plus a full ReefDose plan and ReefRun program editor and ReefMat settings (beta) ReefControl , ReefControl Power , ReefWave , ReefLED (beta) ReefControl's probes. ReefControl Power's sockets as outlets, on or off, no automatic mode yet. ReefWave and ReefLED, view only Jecod Pump mode and intensity, and its day program Maxspect (beta) Mode and speed for Gyre A and Gyre B , Pump health (cleaning countdown, head A current, fitted heads, firmware), and its schedule, view only GHL ProfiLux / Mitras (beta) Probes, sockets, dosers, level sensors and, on the Director models, KH and ion test results HYDROS (beta) Whatever its device key reports: inputs, and with a write key, outputs, modes, dosing heads and tester commands If a Red Sea unit stops itself, its page tells you what's wrong and puts the fix right next to it. That's Resume , Clear emergency , Sensor cleaned , I already loaded a new roll , or Reset for a dosing head. A ReefDose plan, a ReefRun speed program and ReefMat's scheduled advance, model, position and New roll all work the same way here as on your phone. Connecting your equipment and Controlling your equipment have the detail. DŌS heads You have to measure a DŌS head once before Cora will dose with it by hand. Measure to dose runs the head for twenty seconds into a measuring container, and you enter how much came out. Cora keeps one measurement per head and uses the newest, whichever Cora Max took it. The head's page shows where and when it was measured. After a manual dose, a head you'd set to Off in Apex Fusion stays Off. Any other head goes back to Auto. What a head is used for In a head's settings sheet you can set its use type . The options are Supplement , Water change: new saltwater in , Water change: old water out , Kalkwasser , Calcium reactor , Food or Top-off , and Other . The use type changes two things. How big a container it can track. A Supplement head tracks up to 20 litres. Every other use type can track a container of up to 500 litres, so a head running a water change or a calcium reactor isn't treated like a small dosing bottle. Whether it can take a large dose by hand. Supplement and Food heads keep today's small, careful ceiling. Every other use type can have its own Largest dose by hand limit, up to a hard ceiling of 10 litres, and its own daily limit for automations and the Assistant . A large hand dose also needs Large doses (Beta) turned on in the head's settings, off by default: turn it on only after you've watched the first large dose run at the tank. You can link a water-change pair (new saltwater in, old water out) as a Paired head and set a Balance warning above amount. If the two heads' totals for the day drift apart by more than that, Cora warns you. A pair that's out of balance usually means one side isn't pumping as it should. If a large dose is interrupted A large dose changes what the head is doing on the Apex for a while, then puts its normal schedule back. If the connection drops partway through, Cora Max shows a banner on that head's page: "A large dose on [head] did not finish cleanly. Cora keeps trying to put its program back; check it in Apex Fusion." Check the head in Apex Fusion yourself, then tap I checked the head in Fusion to clear the banner. Only do this once you've confirmed that the head's own schedule is running, not Cora's dosing program. If the banner won't clear, or keeps coming back, have a look at Troubleshooting . GHL ProfiLux and Mitras GHL support is in beta We're still testing and developing GHL support. Some readings or controls may not work yet, and what you see here may change between updates. Connect a GHL controller from your phone: Devices → Add Device → GHL . Connecting your equipment has the steps. Cora Max shows and controls it once a Cora Max on its network has read it, but setup itself happens on the phone. A ProfiLux mini reads its probes, sockets, dosers and level sensors. With Allow control from Cora (Beta) on, a mini can also switch its sockets, the same way as any other GHL controller. Everything else, such as setpoints and feed pause, needs a ProfiLux 3, 4 or Mitras. Controls stay off until you turn on Allow control from Cora (Beta) on the device's page. It's off by default. Once it's on, a socket can be set to Always on , Always off , or Back to automatic , and a setpoint such as temperature or pH shows its allowed range and refuses a value outside it. Both kinds of change are saved on the controller itself and stay there even if Cora later loses touch with it. A change that looks like it touches a heater or return pump asks you to confirm twice. If a doser's container is running low, Cora warns you the same way it does for other consumables. The default is 20% full, and you can change it from the doser's rule in the Alert Center . If the controller won't take a change, its GHL API is probably switched off. GHL turns this off after every firmware update; turn it back on from System → GHL API in GHL Control Center or GHL Connect. Troubleshooting has the rest. HYDROS HYDROS support is in beta We're still testing and developing HYDROS support. Some readings or controls may not work yet, and what you see here may change between updates. HYDROS is the only integration that reaches its controller through the cloud, so it works even when Cora Max is on a different network than the controller. It's set up only from your phone: Devices → Add Device → HYDROS . Connecting your equipment has the steps. Reading and controlling it works the same as on your phone; see Controlling your equipment for outputs, modes, dosing heads and tester commands, and for the per-head dose limits. Schedules You can write Jecod pump day programs at the wall as well as on your phone. The editor is the same, with a day graph, a list of periods and a row of actions. More about this in Scheduling equipment . You can view a Maxspect gyre's schedule (beta) here, but you can't save it. Set it in the Maxspect app. Outlets You can also reach outlets from the Outlets & Feed drawer at the bottom of the dashboard. It lists the outlets turned on for this dashboard (or all of them, if you haven't picked any). More about this in Outlets and controls . DŌS heads never show up in the outlet list, so you can't switch one on there and leave it running. Dose from the head's own page. A large Apex with several modules shows all of its outlets and probes. Consumables You set refill thresholds (reagent, containers, reservoirs) on the device's own page here, the same as on your phone. More about this in Consumables . Logging and calculating at the tank Two things are often easier at the wall than on a phone. Log parameters lets you type test results on the on-screen keyboard. It's in the tank menu. Dose calculator works out a correction from the tank's volume and your product strengths. Open it from a parameter's page. It uses the same volume and product strengths as your phone, so a dose worked out here matches one worked out there. More about this in Dosing . On a second Cora Max When more than one Cora Max shows a tank, one of them reads that tank's equipment. The device pages call it the Cora Max at the tank. The others can still open the device pages, and a status tag reading Cloud means you're on one of them. They show what the Cora Max at the tank last read and how long ago. Each command goes through Cora Cloud to the Cora Max at the tank, which carries it out. A few things only work on the Cora Max at the tank. Measure to dose and Re-measure only show up there. Once a head is measured, Dose now works from any Cora Max. You can change a Jecod schedule from another Cora Max only if the Cora Max at the tank has read the pump in the last hour, and never for a pump that only talks over Bluetooth. One Apply to the pump from there sends at most 12 changes, so send a bigger edit in parts. What was changed, and by what Every action is logged along with what caused it. More about this in Activity and timeline .

d: What Cora Max can see, which device reads each tank, and what to check when readings stop.
b: Settings → Devices lists the equipment Cora Max can see and how each device is doing. The device list Filter by tank, then each device with a one-line summary of what it holds. Cora Max sees the same equipment as your phone, because they both read the same account. Use the filter chips at the top to show All tanks or just one. Each entry has a status dot, a one-line summary of what the device holds ( 21 outlets · 4 feeds , 19 tests left ) and the tank it belongs to. Cora Max shows and controls devices, but every device is added, assigned and removed from your phone. With no devices yet, this screen says Add devices in the Cora app . More about adding equipment in Adding, editing and removing devices . Primary Cora Max: which device talks to your equipment The Primary Cora Max is the Cora Max (or other Cora device) that reads a tank's controller and other equipment for the whole account. Each tank only needs one device doing this. Every other screen shows what it reads. To see or change it, open Settings → [your tank] → Primary Cora Max . You have two options. Any active (automatic) means every online Cora device that can reach this tank's equipment shares the work, and the latest write wins. Use this unless you have a specific reason to pin one device. Pin one device means only that device reads the equipment. If it goes offline, nothing reads this tank's equipment until you pin a different one or switch back to Any active (automatic). You set this once for the tank, and it applies to every Cora screen. You can change it from any Cora Max that shows the tank, or from Cora Mobile. More about this in More than one Cora device . Primary Cora Max and Cora Assistant are two separate settings Primary Cora Max decides which device reads your equipment . Cora Assistant decides which device answers "Hey Cora" . If you have more than one Cora Max, you can set them separately. More about this in Talking to Cora . If a tank's readings stop If one tank's readings stop while another tank on the same screen keeps updating, start here. Open Settings → [that tank] → Primary Cora Max . Check that a device is assigned and that it's online. If another Cora Max for this tank shows Main Cora offline in its top bar, the primary has lost its connection. What the status tag means is explained in The Cora Max home screen . Settings → Cora Max Settings → Network & Updates → Device polling shows how often this Cora Max reads your devices. You can only view it here. It's set from Cora Mobile. If that doesn't help, have a look at Troubleshooting . Managing a Cora Max from your phone Open the Cora Max from the Devices tab on your phone. You'll see its variant, firmware version and when it was last seen. You can also rename it or change some of its settings without walking over to it. Polling interval, brightness, volume, on-screen alerts and dim timer. These settings only affect that one screen (its brightness, volume, on-screen alert banners and dim timer), just as if you'd changed them at the wall. Turning off on-screen alerts doesn't change alert history or push notifications. Which tanks a Cora Max shows, and which device is its Primary Cora Max for each tank, apply to the whole account. You can change them from either device, as described above. Check device health before changing anything The Status section of Settings → Cora Max Settings on this screen shows polling status, last poll time and last cloud write for each tank. It doesn't change anything. Use it to find out what's going on before you change a setting.

d: The daily briefing, ICP results, health reports and history charts on Cora Max.
b: Cora Max shows the same insights as your phone, on a screen big enough to read from across the room. You'll find them in the tank menu (tap the tank name in the top bar). The briefing at full size. Reef Buddy The daily briefing shows up on the dashboard and also has its own full screen. There you'll see the Stability and Data scores, the summary and the insights behind them. What the scores mean is explained in Reef Buddy . ICP results Every uploaded result, with its score. This screen shows your uploaded results with the score and summary for each, plus trends across all your reports. The score out of 100 comes from comparing your results with their ranges. If any parameter is out of range, the score can't go above 70. If one is far out of range, it can't go above 40. The colour shows the band. Green (healthy) is above 70, amber (needs attention) is 40 to 70, and red (critical) is below 40. You upload results from your phone. More about this in ICP and health reports . Health reports You can run and read a health report at the wall. It's the same assessment your phone makes, and its score works the same way as an ICP score. History charts You can open any parameter as a full-screen chart, with the same time ranges as your phone. On a wall display, this is the best way to spot a slow drift. A month of alkalinity at full screen shows a trend a small tile can't. The chips pick which readings to show: All , Apex , Manual , ICP , Cora , ReefBeat or AquaWiz . Each source has its own colour, and the chips work as the key. ReefBeat and AquaWiz points are squares, and readings someone took by hand (Manual and ICP) are larger dots. All shows every source side by side and never averages one source's readings with another's. Guided journeys You can follow a journey on Cora Max and see how far along it is. You can also take readings for a cycling journey here. Log a test on the cycling screen records ammonia, nitrite and nitrate without reaching for your phone, which helps when you're at the tank with a test kit in hand. At the wall, an issue journey is view only. Starting one, completing a step, recording an outcome, and resolving or dismissing it all happen on your phone. More about this in Guided journeys .

d: The record-keeping screens on Cora Max, and when to use them instead of your phone.
b: Cora Max shows the same records as your phone, but you can't edit all of them here. What you can do at the wall depends on the area. Area On Cora Max Journal Read and add entries Readings Log test results with the on-screen keyboard Maintenance Complete or snooze a task. You create and edit tasks on your phone Livestock View only. Add and edit on your phone Anything you add here shows up on your phone right away, and the other way round. You'll find all of them in the tank menu (tap the tank name in the top bar). Tasks due, with Snooze and Done on each, and what was completed recently. Journal You can add an entry without leaving the tank. You're usually standing at the wall screen when you do the work anyway. Open the tank menu (tap the tank name in the top bar) and tap + to add an entry. Or say "Hey Cora, log that I fed mysis." More about this in The journal . There's no journal icon in the top bar The icon next to the devices icon is Reef Buddy , and its dot means today's briefing is unread. You add journal entries from the tank menu or by voice. Livestock This is the full inventory, grouped by type, with the same statuses as on your phone. It's view only here. You add and edit livestock in Cora Mobile, and what you add there shows up on this screen right away. More about this in Livestock . Maintenance This is the task list with its compliance figure and overdue count. You can mark a task done as soon as you finish it. More about this in Maintenance . Logging readings Cora Max has an on-screen keyboard for typing in test results, so you can record a test at the tank where you did it. One set of records Each tank has one journal, one livestock inventory and one maintenance list. Cora Max and your phone show the same records.

d: The multi-tank overview screen, and how to move between tanks on Cora Max.
b: If Cora Max shows more than one tank, the Reef Room gives you an overview of all of them. Open it with the grid icon at the far left of the top bar. On screen, it's called Cora Tanks . Each tank with its health score, headline parameters and anything out of range. The layout A Cora Max shows up to four tanks , and the Reef Room gives each one an equal share of the screen. Tanks Layout 1 No Reef Room. The screen opens right on that tank 2 Side by side 3 Three across 4 Two by two Four tanks is the limit You can assign at most four tanks to a Cora Max, both when you pair it and later from Devices → your Cora Max . If you try to add a fifth, you'll be asked to remove one first. If you have more tanks than that, use a second screen. Each one keeps its own set. What a tile shows Each tile sums up one tank. A health score in a ring. Next to it is a line like 3 of 37 parameters out of range (or All 37 parameters in range ), and how many are near their limits. An out-of-range chip when something needs attention. Four key parameters with recent trends. When it last updated , and a link to that tank's dashboard. The health score looks at how far out each parameter is and how much it matters, so lots of good readings can't hide one serious problem. It only reads 100% when nothing is out of range. If a major parameter like alkalinity, calcium or magnesium is far out of range, the score can't go above 33%. A heavy metal far out of range can bring it down to 0%. Parameters near their limits are counted on the tile but don't lower the score. Under the tiles, a ticker shows each tank's current health headline in turn. You can tell which tank needs attention from across the room without touching the screen. Moving between tanks Tap a tile , or Open dashboard , to go to that tank. Swipe sideways on the dashboard to move between tanks and back to the Reef Room. The grid icon takes you back to the Reef Room from any tank page. You won't see it on the Reef Room itself. Each tank has its own dashboard layout, so the screen changes completely as you move between them. More about this in Editing the Cora Max dashboard . Single-tank systems With one tank paired, Cora Max opens right on that tank's dashboard and there's no Reef Room page.

d: The Settings screen on Cora Max, with household settings, each tank, and everything about this screen itself.
b: Open settings with the gear at the far right of the top bar. Cora, then your tanks, then Cora Max Settings. Settings has three groups. CORA holds things that apply to all the Cora devices in your household. TANKS has one row per tank. And there's a single Cora Max Settings row for everything about this screen alone. Two kinds of setting Some settings belong to your account . They're the same whichever phone or Cora Max you look at, and changing one changes it everywhere. Others belong to this screen only, like its brightness or Wi-Fi. The CORA and TANKS groups are account settings. Cora Max Settings, the third group, holds this screen's own settings. CORA These apply to every Cora device on your account. Row Opens Automations Every scene for all your tanks, with a filter by tank. More in Scenes on Cora Max Devices The equipment Cora controls, for all your tanks. More in Devices and device health Cora Assistant Which device answers when someone says "Hey Cora." More in Talking to Cora TANKS Each tank has a row that opens its own settings. Alert thresholds sets the healthy range for each metric. More in Alerts and thresholds . Units picks the units this tank uses for salinity, temperature, alkalinity, volume, phosphate and nitrate. With Auto , each reading shows in the unit its source recorded it in. If you pick a specific unit, everything on this tank is converted to it, on every screen and when the Assistant speaks. Primary Cora Max is the device that reads this tank's equipment. More in Devices and device health . Dashboard layout is this tank's Cora Max layout. More in Editing the Cora Max dashboard . This tank's records and reports are here too: Journal , Maintenance , Livestock , Reef Buddy , Health Reports and ICP Reports . Cora Max Settings: everything about this screen The last row in Settings carries this Cora Max's name. It opens everything that applies to this screen only , in these groups. Group Covers Display Brightness, dim-after timer and its brightness, night dimming, showing the clock, and waking the screen on an alarm Sound & Voice Audio output (internal speaker, 3.5 mm or Bluetooth), the alert chime and its volume, spoken alerts, and Wake-word listening on or off Reef Buddy The hour the daily briefing arrives (one setting for the account, the same as on your phone), and whether it's read aloud Child Lock On or off, and how long before it locks. How to unlock it is in Talking to Cora Notifications Notification history, the inbox for your whole account with every briefing, alarm and account notice Language The one language your whole account uses. See the note below Network & Updates Wi-Fi, firmware updates, and a view-only line showing how often this Cora Max reads your devices (set from Cora Mobile) Status One card for each tank this screen shows, with polling status, last poll and last cloud write. View only Help & About Help & Support, and About (version and Licenses ) Reset Re-pair this device, and factory reset Language applies to your whole account When you change Language , every phone and every Cora Max on your account switches with it. New reports, alerts and briefings come in the new language. Reports and alerts you already have stay in the language they were written in and aren't translated again. Alarms and their recoveries, newest first, across every tank. Recoveries are logged as well as alarms. So when a parameter goes out of range and comes back, you see both halves instead of a warning with no follow-up. Pairing, re-pairing and factory reset Cora Max Settings → Reset shows what this screen is paired to right now, and gives you two options. Re-pair this device clears this screen's pairing and takes it back to the pairing screen. Factory reset also clears every preference saved on this screen. Its confirmation tells you exactly what's cleared and what's kept. Neither one touches the tank data already saved to Cora Cloud. Both remove this Cora Max from your account and make it forget its Wi-Fi network, so you pair it again from Cora Mobile like a new one. If Cora Max can't reach Cora Cloud to remove itself, it tells you it's still listed in Cora Mobile. Open it there under Devices and choose Remove device . The dialog shows what's cleared and what's kept before you go ahead. A reset clears the screen, but your data stays Factory reset removes the pairing and every setting stored on the device, and takes it back to its pairing screen. Tank data already saved to your account is kept. Pair the device to a tank again and it comes back. What you lose is this screen's own setup, like its Wi-Fi, display, sound and voice settings. You may get your layouts back Before a reset, Cora Max saves a copy of its configuration. If you pair it back to the same tank , it offers Restore previous layout for this tank? Take it, or choose Start fresh if you wanted a clean screen. Which tanks this screen shows A Cora Max can show one tank or several, and you switch between them from the top bar. You choose which tanks it shows on your phone , under Devices → your Cora Max . Updates Cora Max keeps itself up to date. New versions download in the background and install themselves, and Cora Max tells you what changed. If a version has just arrived, you'll see a prompt on screen. You don't need to do anything to stay current. More in Keeping Cora Max updated .

d: First start, connecting to Wi-Fi, pairing with your account, and getting your tanks onto the big screen.
b: Cora Max is the command centre for your reef room. It's a wall screen that shows your live system, you can read it from across the room, and you can talk to it. Set your tanks up on your phone first Cora Max shows the tanks and devices from your account. If you set them up in Cora Mobile first, Cora Max picks them up as soon as you pair it, and you don't have to type on a wall screen. Dashboard layouts don't carry over, though. Each screen keeps its own, so you arrange this one after pairing. More about this in Editing the Cora Max dashboard . What you need Cora Max, plugged in and on Your Wi-Fi network name and password The account you use for Cora Mobile Setup is driven from your phone Turn Cora Max on. It shows a pairing screen and makes itself visible to your phone. You don't type anything on it. The screen shows its name so you can pick the right one on your phone. The screen shows the name your phone will see, ending in a short code. If you're pairing more than one, that code tells them apart in the list on your phone. Everything else happens in Cora Mobile, in five steps you can see across the top of the sheet: Connect · WiFi · Auth · Tanks · Done. 1 · Connect. On your phone, tap Devices → Add Device → Cora . It finds Cora Max and shows its MAC address, firmware version, variant and hardware revision, so you can check it's the right one before you go on. 2 · WiFi. Pick your network from the list, or tap Rescan , then enter the password on your phone's keyboard. 3 · Auth. Your phone links Cora Max to your account. Cora Max shows its own progress while this happens. The screen follows the account check while your phone runs it. 4 · Tanks. Choose which tanks this screen manages, up to four . Each one is listed with its name and type. 5 · Done. Cora Max confirms it's set up and gives you a Recovery PIN . Write the Recovery PIN down The last step shows a six-digit Recovery PIN . It's the only way into recovery on that Cora Max. To use it, hold five fingers on the top-right corner of the screen for ten seconds, then enter the PIN. You can find it again later in that device's settings on your phone, but not on Cora Max itself. Pairing links the screen to your account Once it's paired, Cora Max sees the same tanks, devices, readings and records as your phone. Dashboard layouts are the exception. Cora Max builds its own from your tank profile, and you arrange it separately. Follow the on-screen steps to link it to your account. Cora Mobile tells you when pairing has worked. One account, many screens You can pair more than one Cora Max to the same account, say one in the reef room and one somewhere else. Each can show different tanks and have its own dashboard layout. If two show the same tank, Controlling equipment from Cora Max explains what the second one can do with its equipment. Changing which tanks it shows The tanks a Cora Max shows are part of its pairing, and you change them on your phone . Open the Cora Max in Devices and edit its assigned tanks. You can't change them in Cora Max's own settings. Building the dashboard Cora Max builds its own starting layout from your tank profile. It doesn't copy the one on your phone. The easiest way to change it is from your phone, under Devices → your Cora Max → Edit Dashboard . That's quicker than arranging tiles on a wall. The big-screen dashboard works differently from the phone. It's a fixed grid, and everything has to fit on one screen. More about this in Editing the Cora Max dashboard . Updates Cora Max updates itself. When a new version is out, it downloads in the background, installs it and tells you what changed. You can see which version you're on under Settings → Cora Max . Moving it to a different network Go to Settings → Cora Max Settings → Wi-Fi , pick the new network and enter the password. Cora Max stays paired, so you don't need to set it up again.

d: What everything on the Cora Max display means, from the top bar to the dashboard grid and the outlets drawer.
b: Cora Max shows one tank at a time, with live readings filling the screen so you can read them from across the room. One tank, filling the screen. The top bar From left to right: The grid icon opens the Reef Room, the overview of every tank this screen shows. The tank name , with a small arrow. Tap it to open the tank menu , which has every screen for the tank you're looking at, from logging a test result to arranging the dashboard. The full list is below. Alert tags show anything that's out of range right now. If there are more than fit, you'll see +2 (or however many). Tap one to see them all. The clock . The status tag shows what this screen is doing right now. Green means all is well, amber needs a look, and red is a fault. Every status is listed below. Battery and Wi-Fi . The devices icon shows everything connected and how it's doing. The Reef Buddy icon opens today's briefing. A dot means you haven't read it yet. The Cora Assistant icon starts a voice conversation. The gear opens settings. What the status pill means Tag Meaning Online This screen is collecting your readings, and they're up to date Cloud Another Cora is collecting this tank's readings and this screen is showing them. They're just as up to date as with Online . If you have more than one Cora, the one that isn't collecting shows this Polling Apex , Voice active Busy with something right now Polling off Collecting is turned off for this tank. You can turn it back on in Cora Mobile Updating Collecting is paused while an update installs Stale Readings have stopped coming in. The screen shows the last ones it got Apex retry 12s Your Apex didn't answer. Cora Max tries again when the countdown ends Cloud sync failed Your Apex answered, but its readings couldn't be saved to Cora Cloud, so the dashboard falls behind. Cora Max keeps trying Offline No connection. The screen shows the last data it got Offline, retrying in 45s Your network is up, but Cora Cloud has been out of reach for more than 30 seconds. Cora Max reconnects by itself, and the countdown shows when it tries next Main Cora offline This screen is a second Cora Max for this tank, and the Primary Cora Max (the one pinned to read this tank's equipment) has gone offline. This screen keeps showing the last data it has until the primary comes back or you choose a different Primary Cora Max. More in More than one Cora device Apex password Your Apex turned down the saved password. Have a look at Troubleshooting How the retry countdown works Cora Max tries to reconnect at a steady pace. It waits about 15 seconds after the first drop, then 15 seconds again, then 30 seconds twice, then once a minute until it gets through. It never gives up. Offline, retrying in 45s is normal. Cora Assistant starts listening right away Tapping the Cora Assistant icon starts a live voice session. If you wanted settings, that's the gear on the far right. The dashboard The rest of the screen is the dashboard, a fixed grid that keeps every widget visible. It doesn't scroll. Widgets work the same as on your phone, but big enough to read from a few steps back. What each shape shows is in the Widget reference . To change what's on the dashboard, see Editing the Cora Max dashboard . Every widget with a measured parameter shows its age and source , just like on your phone. A number with 2d next to it is two days old. Device and control tiles show their own state instead. The tank menu Everything for the current tank, from the tank name in the top bar. Tap the tank name to open the menu for the tank on screen. Item Opens Log parameters Type in test-kit readings on the on-screen keyboard Journal The journal for this tank Reef Buddy The latest briefing Health Reports Health assessments Maintenance The task list ICP Reports Uploaded lab results Alerts The healthy range for each metric on this tank Livestock This tank's inventory , view only on this screen Activity Every outlet, feed and dose , and what happened Dashboard layout Arrange the widgets on this screen Tank settings The full settings screen for this tank Switching tanks Tap the grid icon at the far left of the top bar to go to the Reef Room , then open the tank you want. Each tank has its own dashboard layout, so the whole screen changes as you switch. The Outlets & Feed drawer Pull up the tab at the bottom of the screen to open a drawer with every outlet on the system and the feed controls. Outlets can each be switched between Auto, Off and On. Feed pauses the right equipment while you feed and puts it all back afterwards. This drawer controls real equipment Everything here acts on your equipment. A command goes out the moment you tap, but sending it doesn't mean it's done. It comes back Confirmed, Unconfirmed, Refused or No change, and you can see which in Activity . Feed mode is the safe way to pause flow for feeding, because it puts everything back by itself. A manual Off stays off until you change it back. If something looks out of place If readings look stale, or the status tag is amber or red, start with Troubleshooting .

d: How Cora Max updates itself, and what happens if an update goes wrong.
b: Automatic updates Cora Max keeps itself up to date. New versions download in the background and install themselves, and Cora Max tells you what changed. You don't need to do anything to stay current. Checking the version Firmware Update, in the Network & Updates section of Cora Max Settings. Go to Settings → Cora Max Settings → Firmware Update (in the Network & Updates section) to check for and install updates, and to set the update channel and schedule. Further down the same screen, the Status section shows each tank's polling status, last poll and last cloud write. When an update is available A prompt tells you what's new and gives you two choices. Update now installs right away and restarts. Snooze 3 hours asks you again later. If you leave it, the update installs itself overnight, roughly between 3 and 5 in the morning, so the screen doesn't restart while you're looking at it. You don't lose readings during an update Your data lives in your account. When Cora Max restarts, it comes back with the same tanks, dashboards and history. Recovery Recovery is a maintenance mode for when Cora Max won't start normally, or when you need to fix its setup without a laptop. To get in, hold five fingers on the top-right of the screen for about ten seconds , then enter the Recovery PIN . You saw that six-digit PIN when you paired Cora Max, and it's also in that device's settings in Cora Mobile. Cora Max itself never shows it, so a guest or a child leaning on the screen can't get into recovery. From recovery you can: Fix the Wi-Fi connection Re-pair Cora Max to your account Force a firmware update Factory reset Cora Max If Cora Max fails to start several times in a row, it can also roll itself back to the previous version. A screen in recovery isn't controlling anything Your controller keeps running its own programming. But an automation step that this Cora Max has to carry out can't run while it's in recovery. The rule fires, but the step never reaches the equipment. If a unit does not restart Email cora@coraiq.tech with the version shown on screen and the message it shows. Don't re-pair it first. The pairing state often helps work out what happened.

d: Using voice on Cora Max, from starting a conversation to what you can ask and how confirmations work.
b: You can talk to Cora Max. It's the easiest way to use it when your hands are wet or you're across the room. Two ways to start Say "Hey Cora" . Cora Max listens in the background for the wake phrase and starts a session when it hears it. Or tap the Cora Assistant icon in the top bar. Cora starts listening right away, answers out loud, and keeps listening until you stop it. You can turn off wake-word listening and still tap to talk. Settings → Cora Max Settings → Sound & Voice → Wake-word listening turns background listening off. Tapping the Cora Assistant icon still works, so use this if you'd rather the screen wasn't listening all the time. Audio output , in the same Sound & Voice section, picks the internal speaker, a 3.5 mm connection or Bluetooth. For voice, the internal speaker is the weakest of the three. Which device answers "Hey Cora" If you have more than one Cora Max at home, only one of them answers the wake phrase. That's the Answering device . It's a separate setting from the device that reads your equipment, which is the Primary Cora Max (more in Devices and device health ). Change it in Settings → Cora Assistant on any Cora Max, or in Cora Mobile. It applies to your whole household. It starts the moment you tap Cora Assistant starts a live session right away, with no confirmation step. If you tapped it by mistake, stop the session. Nothing is lost. What to ask Questions about the tank: "What's my alkalinity?" "Has the temperature been stable today?" "When did I last change water?" "Why is pH lower than usual?" "Compare the last six months of my magnesium with my latest ICP." Things to do: "Turn the skimmer off." "Start feed mode." "Put the fan back on auto." "Log that I did a twenty litre water change." You don't need to repeat yourself for follow-ups. After a question about the display tank, "and the frag tank?" works. Child lock Settings → Cora Max Settings → Child Lock stops anyone switching equipment from this screen. Questions and readings still work. Cora will tell you your alkalinity, but it won't switch the return pump off. Turn it on for a screen that children or visitors can reach. To unlock it, either: press the volume key three times within two seconds , or hold five fingers in the top-right corner for ten seconds . All three presses have to fit inside two seconds. This keeps casual taps from unlocking the screen. Child lock isn't a security lock, though. Anyone who sees how you unlock it can do the same. Confirmations Before anything reaches your equipment, Cora checks with you. It tells you exactly what it's about to do and waits for your OK. If what you said could mean more than one thing (you have two heaters and said "the heater"), Cora asks which one instead of guessing. Confirming is your call The confirmation is there so nothing catches you by surprise. Read it before you agree, especially for anything that switches off life support. What Cora can see The same as on your phone, for the tank on screen. That's your live readings and how old each one is, up to about six months of history for any parameter, your journal and your lab results. If a reading is stale, Cora tells you so and doesn't treat it as current. Which tank Cora is talking about It's whichever tank the screen is showing. Switch tanks in the top bar first, or name the tank in your question. Stopping Say "stop" , or tap to end the session. Cora stops listening when the session ends. If it mishears Reef words are hard, and equipment names are harder. If Cora keeps mishearing a device, rename it in Devices to something more distinct. Short, everyday words work best. If Cora doesn't respond Check that Wake-word listening is still on ( Settings → Cora Max Settings → Sound & Voice ), that this Cora Max is your Answering device (see above), and that its volume is up. A noisy sump or a filter right next to Cora Max can also stop it hearing the wake phrase. Moving it, or speaking a bit closer, usually fixes that. If that doesn't help, have a look at Troubleshooting .

d: Sign in, reset a forgotten password, and fix an email address you can't verify.
b: Your account keeps your tanks, readings and devices together. This page covers signing in and getting back into your account. Creating an account When you sign up, check I agree to: Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy before Cora creates your account. Both are links, so you can open and read them first. Ways to sign in You can sign in with an email address and password , or with Continue with Apple or Continue with Google . Use the same method every time. If you created your account with an email address and then sign in with Google, you'll land in a second, empty account. Your tanks aren't gone. You're just in the wrong account. Sign out and sign in again the way you did the first time. Forgotten password On the sign-in screen, tap Forgot password? , enter your email address and tap Send Link . Open the link on the same device and set a new password. The message is the same either way You'll see "if that address has a Cora account, a reset link is on its way" , whether or not the address is registered. This stops anyone using the screen to find out who has an account. If no email arrives, you probably signed up with a different address.
